title: Molecular Profiling to Predict Response to Treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
summary:
MP2PRT-ALL is the strongest treatment-response resource in this corpus, and it is not widely known. Every one of the 1,510 patients has a populated treatment outcome, a named regimen or line of therapy, and a progression status at follow-up - 100% coverage on all three, which is rarer than it sounds. Median follow-up is 100.2 months with a maximum of 180.8, the longest realised follow-up of any cohort indexed here. Whole genome sequencing covers 1,507 cases, exome 1,494 and RNA sequencing 1,479.
Because the cohort is drawn from cooperative-group trials, the treatment is protocolised rather than heterogeneous, which removes the confounding that usually defeats treatment-response analysis in observational cohorts. 333 of 1,510 patients are recorded as Hispanic or Latino, a group with documented excess ALL incidence and inferior outcomes and one that is under-represented in most genomic cohorts.
one_liner: 1,510 children with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia from Children's Oncology Group trials, with whole genome sequencing, 8.4 years of median follow-up, and a named treatment regimen and response recorded for every single case.

useful_for.question: Which genomic features predict failure of protocolised induction therapy in paediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia?
useful_for.rationale: Treatment outcome and regimen are populated for 100% of 1,510 cases, and regimen strings name the actual protocol arm, so response can be modeled within a treatment context rather than across an uncontrolled mixture of therapies. Whole genome sequencing on 1,507 cases supports genome-wide discovery at this sample size.
useful_for.statistical_note: Complete response is the dominant outcome category in a curable disease, so the informative contrast is relapse and residual disease rather than induction failure. Expect a heavily imbalanced outcome and plan the design accordingly.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Do Hispanic or Latino children carry a different genomic landscape or a different response profile, and does genomics explain any of the known outcome disparity?
useful_for.rationale: 333 of 1,510 patients are recorded as Hispanic or Latino - both a substantial absolute number and a substantial share, which is unusual. With treatment held closer to constant by the trial protocol, the ethnicity contrast is less confounded by care access than in an observational cohort.
useful_for.statistical_note: Ethnicity is self-reported and unknown for 49 cases. Genetic ancestry can be estimated from the germline data and is the more defensible variable for biological claims; report both and do not treat them as interchangeable.

useful_for.question: What are the long-term survival determinants in paediatric ALL, given follow-up that extends beyond fifteen years?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 84% of cases and median follow-up is 100.2 months, so late relapse and long-term survival are genuinely observable rather than censored away. Very few genomic cohorts of this size reach this follow-up duration.
useful_for.statistical_note: 16% of cases have uninformative vital status; check whether missingness is associated with treatment arm before assuming it is uninformative censoring.

useful_for.question: How do subtype-defining fusions and copy number alterations interact with assigned risk group and delivered therapy?
useful_for.rationale: Structural variant and copy number calls exist for 1,504 cases, and the regimen field records the risk-stratified arm each patient received, allowing molecular subtype to be crossed with the therapy actually delivered.

limitations.statement: Despite complete treatment-outcome coverage, the descriptive treatment fields are empty: treatment type, treatment given and therapeutic agents are all at 0%. The regimen field names the protocol arm, so the therapy is recoverable from trial documentation, but individual drug exposures are not recorded per patient here.
limitations.mitigation: Map the regimen strings onto the published COG protocol definitions to recover drug composition, and state that mapping explicitly in your methods.

limitations.statement: Participants are enrolled on cooperative-group trials, which select for access to a participating center and for eligibility criteria that exclude some patients. Outcomes in trial populations are generally better than in the wider patient population.
limitations.mitigation: Frame results as applying to trial-enrolled patients.
